description.narrative: It is aimed that by 2030, PCAsia contributes to an improvement in the performance of the target Parliaments Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar (currently suspended) and ASEAN Inter- Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA)- by helping to strengthen the capacity of parliamentary staff, and by increasing the intensity of technical exchanges and experience-sharing among their regional peers. There are three indicators as follow: 1) Parliamentary staff provide more effective support to Parliamentarians to perform legislative review, representation and oversight. 2) Parliamentarians perform their core functions of legislation, representation and oversight more effectively. 3) Stakeholders are increasingly satisfied with parliamentary performance.

Det övergripande målet för projektet är att förbättra och utveckla en rad PCAsia-aktiviteter relaterade till kapacitetsutvecklingen av ASEAN:s interparlamentariska församlings (AIPA) medlemsparlament om parlamentariskt arbete. Detta bidrar också till en förbättring av parlamentens prestationer i Sydostasien genom att bidra till att stärka kapaciteten hos parlamentarisk personal och genom att öka intensiteten i tekniskt utbyte och erfarenhetsutbyte mellan deras regionala och internationella kamrater.

The overall objective of the Project is to improve and develop a range of PCAsia activities related to the capacity development of the ASEAN Inter-parliamentary Assembly (AIPA) Member Parliaments on parliamentary works. This also contributes to an improvement in the performance of the Parliaments in South East Asia by helping to strengthen the capacity of parliamentary staff, and by increasing the intensity of technical exchanges and experience-sharing among their regional and international peers.

The results are mainly measured on an output level also in 2022. A new M&E system was ready in 2023 and there are efforts now to make more achievements on this in 2024. The examples of achieved outputs were reported as followed:
- PCAsia offered capacity building support to ASEAN Inter-parliamentary Assembly (AIPA) Member Parliaments, covering a wide variety of skills in response to requests from recipient Parliaments. The highlight was PCAsia contributed in preparing for the 43rd AIPA General Assembly, specifically in supporting the Cambodian Parliament to perform their role as Chair. Activities included training on drafting resolution techniques and public policy communication for staff involved in organizing the Assembly. - PCAsia provided organisational and technical support to Women Parliamentarians of the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (WAIPA) in drafting resolutions and held an inter parliamentary consultative workshop on COVID19 responses. - Two specialized training in carried out in 2022 in support of AIPA for the Cambodian national AIPA Secretariat and the Jakarta-based AIPA Secretariat staff. PCAsia and the AIPA secretariat also went on a joint mission to France and Belgium to build their relations and explore further collaboration with one another and with international partners. Meetings included French Senate, National Assembly, Assemblée Parlementaire de la Francophonie, European Council, European Parliament, and East-West Management Institute etc. - Through cooperation with its implementing partners, PCAsia delivered and co-organised 16 capacity development programmes during the reporting period, based on parliamentary requests. Joining these were 652 participants (236 women, 416 men), primarily staff from AIPA Member Parliaments plus the AIPA Secretariats. - For the first time, PCAsia held training face to face in Vientiane Parliamentary Committee Work and Training of Trainers on Parliamentary Research with work underway to secure facilities in Laos to facilitate further training there. - PCAsia continued to mainstream the crosscutting themes of (1) Environment and Climate Change and (2) Gender Equality and a Human Rights-based Approach. This integration included modules as part of the training programmes on research, diplomacy, and fiscal analysis, as well as the production of research, and planning and technical support. - The Knowledge Exchange Conference on Health Emergency Responses co-organised by PCAsia led to the passage of another resolution to form a regional health emergency working group to exchange information between parliaments and CSOs to better coordinate and prepare for the next pandemic. - PCAsia has also met with BBC Media early 2022 to discuss cooperation in 2023. This can be an interesting way for PCAsia to use experienced communicators in their work. There has been the development of a new PCAsia website and Improvement of the parliamentary information network and library catalogue have been carried out. There are also ongoing use and additions to the PCAsia learning management system. All of these digital improvements give PCAsia an advantage for the future and for attracting partners and donors. - There was also an institutional assessment by E & Y carried out in the beginning of 2022 funded by Sida/EU. This has assisted PCAsia in improving its financial regulations, and operations manual. Having a good system in place can attract other donors.
It is important to note both monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) and the funding sustainability strategy have been the SDC and Embassy's dialogue priorities during 2024. The mid term evaluation will also inform the assessment and recommendations of these perspectives to be followed up further.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
